ed7408cebf7f1ade9e94e4b55093d366e682e8a1.identification: StormAttack DNS-labeled resource DLL injector, Windows x86 (2010 build timestamp)
evidence: Entry 0x402674 calls WinMain-like 0x401cb0. The configuration at VA 0x404120 selects mode 3; it calls 0x401900 then shell cleanup 0x401390.

0x401900 generates a GUID basename, writes HKLM Active Setup Installed Components StubPath, copies its own image, changes the copied configuration to mode 4, and launches the copy. Helper 0x401000 copies the image and sets hidden/system attributes (6).

Mode 4 calls 0x401b90, which writes resource 101 of type DLL via 0x402460 and injects it via 0x401150. The injector creates a target process, allocates and writes its DLL path remotely, resolves LoadLibraryA, and calls CreateRemoteThread.
The mode-1 branch calls 0x401260: it deletes and replaces LanmanServer Parameters ServiceDLL with an attacker-controlled System32 DLL path.
0x401390 obtains its own filename and COMSPEC, constructs a /c del command, starts the cleanup process and resumes its thread.

The embedded PE starts at file offset 0x5060; its apparent code region from child offsets 0x1400 through 0x8bff and its declared entry at child offset 0x681a are zero. The embedded PE has no recovered imports or exports. Resource extraction only copies bytes; no decoder reconstructs those missing regions.
ed7408cebf7f1ade9e94e4b55093d366e682e8a1.limitations: The supplied bytes establish unauthorized hidden persistence, injection and self-deletion code even though the embedded DLL is impaired. No working DDoS, Remcos, Elex or WannaCry payload is inferred from strings or the collector filename. Triage URL could not be retrieved; the verdict rests on traced code. No victim deployment or runtime success is assumed.
ed7408cebf7f1ade9e94e4b55093d366e682e8a1.marker: StormAttack injector: hidden persistence, DLL injection, self-delete

8629bc3143cdebd45deac3e2ac134a7d3235b081.identification: module_bank 0.5.0, Python single-file module packer and importer
evidence: forager fetch --all-wheels pkg:pypi/module-bank@0.5.0 recovered the original universal wheel with identical SHA-256.
__init__.py imports the packer, finder and loader classes; cli.py exposes explicit pack/list/deps/delete_source/install commands. No packaged module bank or hidden executable payload is present.
SQLiteModuleImporter._store_module compiles user-supplied module source, marshals bytecode, optionally encrypts with a caller-provided Fernet key, and stores it through SQLiteVFS.

PyArmorEncryption checks availability with import pyarmor, then invokes sys.executable -m pyarmor.cli gen in a temporary directory; it reads the generated source/runtime and removes its temporary build directory. The helper itself is readable source, not PyArmor-protected output.

SQLiteModuleLoader._exec_plain reads local bank bytes, optionally decrypts, unmarshals and execs in the imported module namespace. _exec_pyarmor deploys a native runtime into a temporary directory before evaluating the caller-selected bank module. Finder installation is explicit; temporary runtimes and dependencies are cleaned up at close/exit.

dependencies.py gathers installed distributions using importlib.metadata and RECORD, excludes absolute/traversing entries and supports recursive Requires-Dist selection. These paths collect local dependencies for user-requested packaging, not credentials.

PermissionError guards reject writes to a read-only bank. vfs.add_file writes the module bank and has no Discord webhook relationship. Fernet.generate_key generates a packer key; no victim-file encryption or disk destruction occurs.
8629bc3143cdebd45deac3e2ac134a7d3235b081.limitations: Published-byte agreement is provenance evidence, not proof that every downstream .mbank or dependency is safe. Code import, decryption and obfuscation are dual-use capabilities and remain detected. No unknown downstream bank is judged.
8629bc3143cdebd45deac3e2ac134a7d3235b081.marker: module_bank 0.5.0: declared packer; fix PyArmor import and upload FPs

585308bdf101cbc0e27b40741dbc25ab13422868.identification: Lombiq Node.js Extensions development branch source archive
evidence: Fresh forager fetch of https://codeload.github.com/Lombiq/NodeJs-Extensions/tar.gz/refs/heads/dev is byte-identical to the supplied gzip archive.

MSBuild targets enable pinned pnpm, install declared frontend build dependencies, and run scripts/run-pnpm-script.js. ExecWithMutex subclasses the normal MSBuild Exec task and coordinates concurrent build readers/writers.

compile-scripts.js runs Babel and Terser on configured assets. clean-assets.js removes configured build output with rimraf; copy-assets.js copies configured source globs. Shell calls run user-selected package scripts or the documented build/lint defaults.

GitHub Actions use secrets for checkout, CI cancellation, NuGet publishing and the declared reusable Jira workflow. pull_request_target and secret references are accurately retained; these declarations do not establish secret theft.
585308bdf101cbc0e27b40741dbc25ab13422868.limitations: No deployment context or execution of external reusable workflows/dependencies is asserted. The original-byte review and matching upstream snapshot support ordinary build tooling.
585308bdf101cbc0e27b40741dbc25ab13422868.marker: Lombiq Node.js Extensions: asset build tooling; relocate MSBuild traits

changes.correction: Preserve the original regex as notable Python call syntax. The Discord composite now requires a discord_webhook import and describes co-occurrence, not bound data flow. Its hostile keylog-upload consumer already required the same import, so attack coverage is retained.

changes.reason: Generic key generation, permission-denial expressions and MSBuild task operations/declarations do not establish wiping, HTTP traffic or LOLBin abuse. Preserve matching and criticality; update exact consumers. Remove inappropriate attack mappings inherited from former objective homes.

placement_review.msbuild: Exec Command and executable-command text -> process/create/shell/command-string. Target name, MakeDir element without required arguments and Copy SourceFiles without a required destination -> build/manifest declarations. These do not prove a copy or directory creation. Hostile design-time composites retain all required original relationships.
placement_review.ancestors: Audited old exact IDs and every ancestor directory selector, plus destination ancestors. The broad HTTP/request selectors lose a generic exception expression; broad objectives/impact exclusion in CrystalX loses generic key generation. Neither should use those neutral facts as attack/network evidence. Broad crypto selection retains moved key generation. Destination build selectors already see the MSBuild schema in the relevant XML controls; language scope prevents new JS-only suppressions. No additional broad selectors were added.
placement_review.fixtures: Original PyArmor 9.2.4 wheel, existing Grabvy ransomware, existing Empire and native-thread MSBuild controls, authorized/unchecked moderation controls, plus inert bootstrap and behavior controls. No specimen code was executed.
